propositions: A focused prerequisite-consistency criterion must evaluate subject plan compatibility with each direct prerequisite independently, with coverage routed through PlanRelationSnapshot preload to finders, isolated from general criteria requests, and with no prerequisite IDs or plan text injected into general reviewers.

Prerequisite findings must use a canonical structured four-field UTF-8 identity encoding (version, text, criteria, prerequisite_id) with big-endian length prefixes and SHA-256, distinct from legacy pipe-delimited non-prerequisite finding IDs, so identical text from different prerequisites retain separate IDs.

Every readable pinned prerequisite must receive exactly one closed-schema disposition (consistent|finding|indeterminate with reason codes) with findings carrying their authoritative prerequisite_id; missing, duplicate, or parse-invalid output maps to indeterminate/output-invalid and indeterminate records never assert incompatibility.

Focused Pass-2 verifier must receive each authoritative prerequisite plan block and set prerequisite_attribution_valid to yes only when evidence establishes that exact pair causes the claimed incompatibility, no when attribution is wrong or unsupported, and never na for focused findings, with attribution errors mapped to indeterminate/attribution-invalid before verdict assembly.

Any indeterminate prerequisite record must force top-level unsigned INDETERMINATE verdict, while retained DET blockers remain visibly in the blocking array with coverage.prerequisite_indeterminate=true; general and focused verification index domains must be independently reshaped without shifting each other.

Singleton focused finder recall must reach ≥0.90, false acceptance ≤0.10, coverage completeness 1.00, and attribution error 0.00 as a gated checkpoint before implementing packed batching and verifier calls; packed results must maintain singleton recall and false acceptance thresholds with comparison against a committed baseline including model, corpus digest, and recorded timestamp.
